name: Mansa Musa's hajj
summary: The king of Mali crosses the Sahara to Mecca with a caravan of thousands and so much gold that its price in Cairo stays low for years. Cairo's chroniclers write Mali into the Islamic world's geography, and within fifteen years a crowned African king appears on Mediterranean charts.

stops.note: The caravan leaves the capital of Mali. Niani is one candidate for its site; the capital has not been located for certain.
The last town before the desert.
He gives away and spends so much gold that its value in Cairo falls for years, al-Umari reports.
Out of money, he borrows from Cairo's merchants at high interest for the journey home.
Mali's general has taken Songhay's capital; Musa visits.
Commissions the Djinguereber mosque, said to be designed by the Andalusian poet Abu Ishaq es-Saheli.

informs.note: 'Rex Melly' appears on Dulcert's chart; the Catalan Atlas of 1375 shows Musa holding a gold nugget
